<!-- hermes-sweeper:item=29549 -->
<!-- hermes-sweeper:verdict=close reason=incoherent confidence=high -->
Thanks for documenting the five-layer memory model and the concrete experiments behind it. This automated hermes-sweeper review is closing this tracking item as incoherent because it remains an architecture discussion rather than an actionable issue.

- The body combines several distinct proposals—layer metadata, automatic distillation, contradiction handling, review queues, graph fusion, and injection policy—without selecting one deliverable or defining acceptance criteria.
- Current Hermes supports bounded built-in memory and pluggable memory providers, so a focused follow-up can identify the intended extension surface and validate one concrete behavior.
- The linked prior discussion, #19546, was already closed on the same basis; its maintainer comment specifically notes that the individual proposals should be scoped into separate, testable changes.

A future focused issue or PR can reference this design and specify one behavior, its storage/provider surface, cache-safe lifecycle requirements, and tests.
